title: A little stop. A lot of spring.
summary: A must-do Rhode Island spring stop: Rose Shack in Saunderstown for a host or mother-in-law gift and a family photograph among the flowers.
search: The journalSaunderstown, Rhode IslandFrom the spring family album · October 19, 2026 Rose Shack · A Rhode Island spring favoriteA little stop. A lot of spring.One for your Rhode Island spring list: flowers for a host, a gift for your mother-in-law, and a photograph worth keeping.Some stops deserve a place in the family album as well as the shopping bag.James and Michael, spring flowers, and a photograph I am very glad we took. From an earlier family visit. The spring stopPlan your visitShare the story Put it on the spring list.Yellow tulips. Pink and white hyacinths. A little shed with FLOWERS across the roof. Our photograph from Rose Shack in Saunderstown has the sort of color that makes you forget how recently you were scraping the windshield.And there are James and Michael in the middle of it. James was smaller then; the smile is the part I keep coming back to.For us, this is a must-do Rhode Island stop in spring. Come for something growing, leave with a present, and take a photograph while you are there. It need not become an entire day's itinerary.A gift that looks like spring.Heading to somebody's house? Looking for a gift for your mother-in-law? This is exactly the sort of place I would put on the list. Choose a flowering plant that suits the recipient's space and gardening ambitions. A small pot of color can be quite enough.Ask what is looking its best that week, whether it belongs indoors or outside, and how to care for it. The lovely part is bringing something alive to the door. The useful part is knowing where it should go afterward. The useful detailsFind Rose Shack.2363 Tower Hill Road, Saunderstown, Rhode Island 02874 401-294-6088 · Official website · Map & directionsStill operating: the official website announces its 2026 season and lists daily hours of 8 a.m.–5 p.m., along with annuals, perennials, shrubs, containers, herbs and vegetables. Gift certificates are also listed as available in store or by phone.For a future spring visit, check the season's opening date and hours before setting out. Flower varieties and stock change with the season; the tulips and hyacinths in our earlier photograph are not a promise of today's selection.A practical note: our photograph shows a gravel surface around the outdoor displays. If firm footing or step-free access matters for your visit, call about the route from parking to the plants and checkout. We have not verified restroom or changing facilities.Business information checked October 19, 2026 against Rose Shack's official website. title: Thank you for passing it along.
summary: A thank-you to Maine Parent Federation and Domain Arrivals for helping more readers discover An AUsome Life and its free New England planning tools.
search: From our family · October 15, 2026Thank you for passing it along.A note to the people helping An AUsome Life reach another family. We put a lot of care into the details before a day out: where to go, what to check, what might help, and what still needs a phone call. A useful page only does its job when someone finds it. So we want to thank the people helping that happen. Thank you, Maine Parent Federation.Seeing Maine Parent Federation share our Accessible New England calendar and Caroline’s Cart New England directory on Facebook meant a great deal to us.Those links are meant for ordinary plans: a Saturday outing, a grocery trip, somewhere new to try. Thank you for putting them in front of families who may be looking for exactly that sort of information, and for the work you do alongside Maine families.Thank you, too, for sharing both resources in the Family Connections of Maine Facebook group. A calendar link or a cart lead passed from one family to another can be a useful place to start the next plan. We appreciate you making room for both.Follow Maine Parent Federation on Facebook Thank you, Domain Arrivals.Domain Arrivals included An AUsome Life in its October 3 collection, noticing the New England outings and the practical details that go with them. We appreciate having another route for readers to find the site.There is room here for a beautiful afternoon and the planning that makes it possible. Thank you for pointing people our way.Read the An AUsome Life listing And to everyone who has sent a link to a friend, a parent group, or someone making a plan: thank you. We hope something here makes the next outing a little easier to arrange.With appreciation, An AUsome Life The two free resourcesAccessible New England calendar — browse activities and follow organizer links for current details.Caroline’s Cart directory — researched store leads; call ahead to confirm that a cart is available.Browse recent press & community mentions
